evidence: Keyboard-only verification is required for complete navigation and logical focus order; automated tooling cannot establish keyboard operability alone.
user_impact: Keyboard users may be unable to reach or activate a service path if any control is pointer-only or the focus order is illogical.
recommended_fix: Use native links/buttons, preserve logical DOM order, and add a skip link.

evidence: Verify every Tab stop has a visible focus indicator and that focused controls are not fully hidden by author-created content.
user_impact: Sighted keyboard users may lose track of focus or activate the wrong control.
recommended_fix: Add a consistent :focus-visible treatment and prevent sticky content from obscuring focus.

evidence: The official services page exposes department-wise and service-wise navigation, creating a dense information hierarchy that should be validated with headings and link names.
user_impact: Users with cognitive or screen-reader navigation needs may have difficulty understanding the service structure.
recommended_fix: Use semantic headings, grouped lists, meaningful link names, and predictable navigation.

evidence: The portal FAQ explicitly advertises font increase/decrease and black-and-white/contrast accessibility options; these controls should be keyboard reachable and visibly focused.
user_impact: Keyboard and low-vision users may be unable to use advertised accessibility features if they depend on pointer interaction.
recommended_fix: Implement controls as native buttons with accessible names, visible focus, and deterministic state.

evidence: The portal is a broad public service hub; the starter project separates client UI, HTTP/API, and data access so service features can evolve independently.
user_impact: Tightly coupled UI and persistence increases change risk and makes accessibility testing harder to isolate.
recommended_fix: Keep React components API-focused, route HTTP concerns in the server, and hide persistence behind repositories.
